title: Delegated SSO failover & KMS rotation — acceptance, rollout checklist, and rollback playbook
creator: Emily Chen
description: PRD clarification and acceptance scope for delegated SSO failover behavior, cryptographic key rotation (KMS/HSM), audit-grade RBAC and log immutability for Private/VPC deployments. This ticket consolidates open questions from the Security review (2026-01-22), runtime performance trade-offs (batching vs. synchronous key unwrap), and operational requirements for rollback. The goal is to produce a clear acceptance checklist and an operator runbook that allows an engineering on-call to: (a) safely rotate keys with minimal downtime, (b) validate SSO failover to an alternate IdP with assertion replay protection, and (c) produce audit evidence for customer compliance reviews. The document focuses on production behavior (SLA, test harnesses, evidence artifacts) rather than product UI copy.
acceptance_criteria: SSO failover: When primary IdP is unreachable, platform must auto-route auth requests to configured secondary IdP within 30s without requiring a service restart; assertion replay protection (nonce+timestamp) must be enforced and tests must demonstrate replay attacks are detected and rejected.

Federation metadata: System ingests updated SAML metadata within 5 minutes of upload and updates active trust bundles without dropping existing sessions; test harness must show zero session loss for active tokens during metadata refresh.

RBAC: Role matrix for Private deploys implemented and automated provisioning tested — admin, operator, auditor, readonly — with least-privilege policies. Automated elevation flow (timeboxed sudo) must require two-step approval for production-critical actions and be audited.

KMS rotation: Customer-managed keys (CMK) rotation workflow supports both online rotation (no restart) and queued rotation (with controlled restart); rotation must complete within announced maintenance window (default: 1 hour) and we must provide a simulated rotation runbook demonstrating key rewrap/unwrap across model-serving nodes.

HSM resilience: For on-prem HSMs, operator playbook must include quorum checks and fallback to software-encrypted key cache if HSM becomes unavailable for more than 2 minutes. The fallback must be logged and require immediate follow-up remediation.

Audit logs: All SSO assertions, key rotation actions, admin elevations, and fallback events are recorded to append-only logs with integrity checks (SHA-256 chaining) and retained for minimum 2 years. Audit extraction for a given customer must be exportable as a time-bounded evidence bundle within 24 hours.

Evidence & tests: For each acceptance item there must be an automated test or a manual test script: end-to-end SSO failover simulation (with IdP kill), KMS rotation dry-run, HSM quorum loss simulation, RBAC misuse attempt, and generation of audit evidence bundle. Test outputs (logs, screenshots, artifacts) must be attached to this ticket.

Performance & SLA: Cryptographic operations involved in rotation/unwrapping must not increase median request latency by more than 15% for 95th percentile token generation paths; performance regression test must be included in PR pipeline.

Documentation: Confluence runbook + step-by-step operator checklist created and linked, including escalation contacts, runbook commands, and rollback steps with clear decision points. Customer-facing onboarding doc updated to reflect expected rotation windows and failover semantics.
